answer: A sybil defense ties each identity to a non-transferable record of work that accumulates slowly, like copper laid down layer by layer. New accounts start under a trust cap and earn higher limits only after independent peers verify tasks over time. A reef of unrelated witnesses makes faking hard: accounts that only vouch for one another form a closed cluster whose endorsements never branch outward. When such clustering appears, those accounts are paused for review while their history stays crystal clear for auditors, so one operator cannot cheaply multiply identities to capture rewards.
